key_insight: A structured LLM workflow can automatically generate, validate, and tune an executable multivariable control strategy directly from a dynamic process model.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to faster control-design prototyping for nonlinear plants, with automated code generation and Bayesian tuning of decentralized PI/PF controllers.
method: Decompose control design into constrained LLM code-generation steps: plant interface, normalization, MV-CV pairing, controller specification, simulation, scenario generation, and evaluation.
Execute and validate each generated artifact before proceeding; repair failed steps using validation feedback.
Use Bayesian optimization to tune controller parameters against a closed-loop objective combining tracking and disturbance-rejection errors.
evidence_signal: On a nonlinear gas-preheater benchmark, the workflow produced a physically consistent decentralized PI feedback-feedforward controller, and Bayesian optimization reduced the closed-loop objective by about 26.5% versus the initially generated controller.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated on a single benchmark, so broader validation is still needed to confirm robustness on larger plantwide-control problems.
paper_title: An LLM-Driven Workflow for Automated Process Control Strategy Generation and Tuning from Dynamic Process Models
